title: Versioned skill bundle runtime
description: Objective: make skills a first-class deterministic input to Moe-next rather than copied old-Moe workspace scaffolding. Deliverable: a focused provider-neutral skill package that validates a closed versioned manifest, resolves only explicitly requested skill IDs and exact digests, enforces bounded file/byte/path limits, snapshots exact skill bytes/assets/provenance into the immutable context/input manifest, and exposes a safe renderer input for provider adapters. Skills are advisory context only and cannot create commands, capabilities, approvals, leases, policy, budgets, effects, or execution authority. Existing .moe/skills files are migration input, not the new runtime contract. Hard dependencies: Runtime contract registry. Owned paths: a new packages/skills/** package and skill-focused tests; adapter wiring and legacy import consume this public contract in their own tasks.
definitionOfDone: The skill manifest, identity, provenance, requested version/digest, file list, and limits are closed, versioned, immutable, and canonical.
Traversal, symlink escape, duplicate or ambiguous identity, unknown fields, oversized counts/bytes, invalid Unicode, missing files, and digest mismatch fail closed with stable errors.
Resolution is explicit and deterministic; exact selected bytes and digests enter context/input/evidence manifests so replay can prove which skill material was used.
Tests prove skill text cannot grant or mutate command, capability, approval, lease, policy, budget, effect, or execution authority; focused typecheck/tests and repository regression checks exit 0.
taskRails: Do not blindly vendor or bless the current .moe/skills tree; treat it as legacy input with recorded provenance.
Provider adapters may render a validated snapshot but must not reinterpret skill text as authority.
Keep contracts, filesystem loading, hashing/canonicalization, and tests in focused modules; target <=250 lines and split before 400.
Use TDD and stage only explicit owned paths; no worktree, broad add, push, merge, reset, or stash.

implementationPlan.description: TDD red — src/skill-manifest.test.ts. Cover, with exact stable-code assertions (result shape is bounded-json style: frozen { ok: false, code, message }; NOT runtime-envelope's {error} shape): (1) closed schema — unknown top-level or per-file key rejects (SKILL_MANIFEST_SCHEMA_INVALID); wrong manifestVersion rejects (SKILL_MANIFEST_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED); (2) bounded-decode mapping — hostile bytes go through decodeBoundedJsonBytes from @moe/contracts and EVERY bounded-json failure code maps to a stable SKILL_* code (invalid UTF-8/Unicode -> SKILL_UNICODE_INVALID; body/depth/string limit -> SKILL_LIMIT_EXCEEDED; syntax/duplicate-key/number/input-type -> SKILL_MANIFEST_BYTES_INVALID), preserving the inner bounded code in the message; (3) identity — skillId charset ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$, version required, digests lowercase 64-hex (reject uppercase/65 chars/non-hex); duplicate skillId (SKILL_IDENTITY_DUPLICATE); (4) path rules, Windows-hardened — reject: absolute, backslash anywhere, ".." segment, "." segment, empty segment, leading "/", ANY colon anywhere (blocks drive letters AND NTFS alternate data streams like "file.md:stream"), any segment whose stem (before first dot, case-insensitive) is a reserved device name CON/PRN/AUX/NUL/COM1-9/LPT1-9 ("CON.md" still resolves to the device), any segment with trailing dot or trailing space (Win32 strips them — defeats duplicate detection), "~" anywhere in a segment (8.3 alias hazard), non-NFC Unicode, path over MAX_SKILL_PATH_CHARS — all SKILL_PATH_INVALID; case-insensitive path collision across entries ("a.md" vs "A.md") -> SKILL_PATH_AMBIGUOUS; (5) limits — file count, per-file byteLength (must be safe nonnegative integer), declared total bytes over caps -> SKILL_LIMIT_EXCEEDED; (6) valid manifest -> ok:true with deep-frozen canonical result and deterministic identity digest (same bytes in -> byte-identical canonical form, key order independent). CRITICAL fixture rule: no hostile fixture string may contain the literals "@moe/scheduler/" or "scheduler/src/" — packages/scheduler/src/package-boundary.test.ts scans ALL of packages/** for those substrings and the repo gate goes red. Run the focused test command and confirm RED (module absent).
implementationPlan.note:
`skill-manifest.test.ts` written, 246 lines, 6 describe blocks. RED confirmed for the RIGHT reason — `Error: Cannot find module './skill-contract.js'`, i.e. the module is absent, not a syntax error masquerading as red.

Read the real bounded-json contract before writing assertions rather than assuming it. `decodeBoundedJsonBytes(input: unknown): BoundedJsonDecodeResult`; failure shape is frozen `{ ok, code, message }`; exactly 9 codes exist (JSON_INPUT_TYPE_INVALID, JSON_BODY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, JSON_UTF8_INVALID, JSON_SYNTAX_INVALID, JSON_DEPTH_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, JSON_STRING_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, JSON_DUPLICATE_KEY, JSON_UNICODE_INVALID, JSON_NUMBER_RANGE_INVALID). Also noted for step 3: decoder objects have a NULL PROTOTYPE and are recursively frozen, so the implementation must use `Object.hasOwn(value, key)` and never a prototype method.

Manifest shape the tests pin: exact top-level keys manifestVersion, skillId, version, origin, files; per-file keys exactly path, sha256, byteLength. Origin is the closed pair "authored" | "legacy-moe-skills", which is how the "legacy .moe/skills is input, not blessed" rail becomes machine-checked rather than prose.

Coverage: closed schema (unknown top-level key, unknown per-file key, missing key, wrong manifestVersion, non-object body); bounded-decode mapping with the inner code preserved in the message (invalid UTF-8 and lone surrogate -> SKILL_UNICODE_INVALID; syntax and duplicate-key and non-byte-array input -> SKILL_MANIFEST_BYTES_INVALID; depth -> SKILL_LIMIT_EXCEEDED); identity (5 bad skillIds, 3 bad digests, empty version, unknown origin, duplicate path -> SKILL_IDENTITY_DUPLICATE); 17 hostile paths plus the length cap; limits (file count, empty list, negative/fractional/oversized byteLength, declared total over cap); canonical identity (key-order independence and content sensitivity).

Two assertions I added beyond the letter of the plan because they cost nothing and close real gaps: an empty `files: []` must be rejected (an empty bundle is not a meaningful skill and would otherwise slip through the count check), and `byteLength: 0` must be ACCEPTED (a legitimately empty file must not be conflated with the empty-list case — this also matters in step 5, where an empty file must serialize as base64 "" rather than an empty typed array).

Every rejection assertion goes through one helper that checks the code AND `Object.isFrozen(result)`, so immutability of the failure object is enforced on all 30-plus rejection paths rather than spot-checked.

Fixture safety verified with the actual boundary regex `/@moe\/scheduler\/|scheduler[\\/]src[\\/]/` over the whole package: 0 matches. My first check used a shell grep that errored with "Trailing backslash" and printed a misleading pass; re-ran it properly with a regex tool. Worth flagging since a false pass here goes red in a foreign package's suite, not mine.

Deep-freeze here recurses plain records/arrays ONLY — it must NEVER receive a typed array (verified: Object.freeze on a Uint8Array with elements THROWS TypeError). All manifest content is strings/integers, so safe. Focused manifest tests green; typecheck green (noUnusedLocals + verbatimModuleSyntax: import type for types).
implementationPlan.note:
GREEN. `pnpm --filter @moe/skills typecheck` exits 0; focused suite 1 file / 52 tests passed. Sizes: skill-contract.ts 160, skill-manifest.ts 222, index.ts 30 — all inside the 250 target.

skill-contract.ts carries the three closed versions, the six frozen limits, the 16-code frozen SKILL_ERROR_CODES tuple, the single `skillFailure` factory (so the frozen `{ok:false, code, message}` shape cannot drift across ~30 rejection sites), sha256Hex, canonical serialization, deepFreeze, and the locally reimplemented guards. Confirmed the plan's claim before relying on it: @moe/contracts exports `decodeBoundedJsonBytes`, `BOUNDED_JSON_ERROR_CODES` and the bounded-json types, but NOT runtime-guards — so isHex64, hasExactKeys, isSafeByteCount, NFC checking are local.

Also added `SKILL_ORIGINS` as a frozen closed pair, "authored" | "legacy-moe-skills". That turns the "legacy .moe/skills is input, not blessed" rail from prose into a machine-checked enum with a test.

TYPE-SYSTEM PROBLEM AND THE FIX, worth recording. My first `canonicalJson(value: CanonicalValue)` failed typecheck with TS2345: a TypeScript `interface` has no implicit index signature, so `SkillManifest` cannot satisfy a recursive `{ readonly [key: string]: CanonicalValue }`. Three ways out: loosen the interfaces to index-signature types (would let arbitrary keys in — defeats the closed schema), hand-convert each interface to a record before hashing (duplication that drifts), or take `unknown` and narrow at runtime. Took the third and made it fail closed: every unsupported runtime shape THROWS (`canonical JSON does not support function`, and non-safe-integer numbers throw too) rather than letting `JSON.stringify` emit `undefined`. A value that cannot be canonicalised can therefore never silently reach a digest. No `any` anywhere.

Two implementation details that carry security weight:
1. `isNormalizedText` checks `value.isWellFormed() && value === value.normalize("NFC")`. The well-formed half is load-bearing on its own — `normalize()` PRESERVES lone surrogates, so an NFC-only check would pass `"\ud800"` straight through into a path or version.
2. Path validation runs entirely before any filesystem call. Colon is rejected anywhere (kills both `C:` drive letters and NTFS `file.md:stream` ADS), reserved device stems are matched on the segment's pre-first-dot stem case-insensitively (so `CON.md` and `docs/nul.txt` are both caught), trailing dot/space are rejected because Win32 silently strips them and would defeat duplicate detection, and `~` is rejected for the 8.3 alias hazard.

Duplicate detection deliberately uses two sets with two DIFFERENT codes: exact-match repeats are SKILL_IDENTITY_DUPLICATE, case-folded collisions are SKILL_PATH_AMBIGUOUS. Order matters — exact is checked first, so `a.md` twice reports duplicate rather than ambiguous.

`deepFreeze` recurses plain records and arrays only and carries an explicit comment that it must never receive a typed array (Object.freeze on a non-empty Uint8Array throws TypeError). Everything in a manifest is strings and integers, so this path is safe today; step 5's base64 strategy is what keeps it safe once real file bytes exist. I will empirically re-confirm the freeze throw in step 7 as the plan requires rather than trusting the note.

implementationPlan.description: TDD red — src/skill-bundle.test.ts (loader + resolution + snapshot + authority). Fixtures via node:fs mkdtempSync under os.tmpdir() (NEVER under the repo root — wrapper auto-commit sweeps strays), rmSync cleanup in afterEach even on failure. Cases: (1) loader reads ONLY manifest-declared files; (2) symlink escape: file symlinked outside bundle root -> SKILL_SYMLINK_ESCAPE (on Windows use fs.symlinkSync file links; if EPERM without Developer Mode, it.skipIf the capability probe fails but keep the containment-logic unit test via injected realpath); root-symlink and sibling-prefix aliasing covered as pure unit tests of the containment predicate: realpath(file) must start with realpath(bundleRoot)+path.sep — assert "D:/x/skills-evil/f" is rejected against root "D:/x/skills"; realpath throwing (missing file) -> SKILL_FILE_MISSING, never an unhandled throw; (3) oversize on disk (actual bytes > declared or > MAX_SKILL_FILE_BYTES) -> SKILL_FILE_OVERSIZED, digest mismatch (bytes differ from manifest sha256) -> SKILL_DIGEST_MISMATCH; read-once contract: bytes are read ONCE, hashed, and those exact bytes enter the snapshot (no re-read window); (4) resolution: requests [{skillId, version, digest}] — unknown id, version mismatch, digest mismatch -> SKILL_REQUEST_UNKNOWN (all-or-nothing: one bad request fails the whole resolution); two loaded bundles claiming same skillId -> SKILL_REQUEST_AMBIGUOUS; empty request list -> ok with empty snapshot (explicit selection means nothing selected); (5) determinism: same inputs -> byte-identical canonical snapshot and identical snapshot digest across two runs and across request order permutations; NO wall-clock anywhere: provenance is content-derived only (skillId, version, per-file sha256, bundle digest, caller-declared origin label "legacy-moe-skills"|"authored") — assert snapshot JSON contains no timestamp-shaped strings and repeated runs are byte-identical; (6) AUTHORITY-NEUTRALITY AS FALSIFIABLE ALLOWLIST (not a denylist): deep-walk snapshot and renderer input asserting (a) every node's Object.keys is an exact subset of a frozen per-node-type allowlist, (b) Object.isFrozen(node) for EVERY node, (c) typeof value !== "function" everywhere, (d) authority === "NONE" and advisoryOnly === true at the root, (e) a hostile skill file whose content is a literal runtime command envelope JSON (schemaVersion/commandKind/leaseAuthority/requestDigest keys) round-trips as inert base64/utf8 STRING content — no envelope-shaped object appears anywhere in snapshot or renderer output. Fixture strings must avoid the scheduler package-boundary literals (step 2 rule). Confirm RED.
implementationPlan.note:
`skill-bundle.test.ts` written, 7 describe blocks. RED confirmed for the right reason — `Cannot find module './skill-loader.js'`; the 52 manifest tests stay green alongside it.

Fixtures use `mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "moe-skills-"))` with an afterEach that drains a root stack via `rmSync(..., {recursive, force})`, so cleanup runs even when a test throws. Nothing is ever written under the repo root — a stray there would be swept into a commit by the wrapper auto-commit.

Loader cases: declared-only reads (a `NOT-DECLARED.md` decoy is written and must not appear), missing file, MISSING BUNDLE ROOT (added beyond the plan — realpath on the root itself throws and must fail closed rather than propagate), digest mismatch, on-disk oversize, and a zero-length file loading as `contentBase64 === ""`. That last one is the empty-file edge the plan flagged: it must load as an empty STRING, never an empty typed array.

Containment is tested three ways so it does not depend on Windows symlink permissions:
1. Injected fs facade proving the sibling-prefix attack fails — realpath `/x/skills-evil/SKILL.md` against root `/x/skills` must be SKILL_SYMLINK_ESCAPE. This is exactly the case a bare `startsWith(realRoot)` would wrongly admit, which is why the implementation must append `path.sep`.
2. The positive case, a file genuinely inside the root, must load.
3. A facade whose realpath THROWS must map to SKILL_FILE_MISSING; asserted with both `.not.toThrow()` and the code, so an unhandled throw cannot pass as a rejection.
Plus a real `symlinkSync` escape test behind a `canSymlink()` capability probe with `it.skipIf`, so it runs where Developer Mode is on and skips cleanly where it is not, without weakening the three above.

Resolution: explicit match on skillId + version + bundleDigest; unknown id, version mismatch, and digest mismatch all SKILL_REQUEST_UNKNOWN; all-or-nothing proven by a two-request case where one good and one bad request fails the whole call; two bundles claiming one skillId is SKILL_REQUEST_AMBIGUOUS; empty request list resolves ok with zero skills.

Determinism: the same two bundles resolved in reversed bundle AND request order must produce an identical snapshotDigest and byte-identical canonicalJson, with output sorted by skillId. Separately asserts the canonical JSON matches no ISO-timestamp regex and contains neither "capturedat" nor "timestamp" — the plan called out `phase0-evidence-contract.ts` capturedAt as the tempting wrong precedent.

AUTHORITY NEUTRALITY IS AN ALLOWLIST, NOT A DENYLIST. A shared `walk()` recurses every node of both artifacts asserting: the node is frozen, its key set is a subset of one of four frozen allowlists (snapshot/renderer/skill/file), and no value is a function. Any key I add later that is not on those lists fails the test — that is the falsifiability a forbidden-key denylist cannot give. On top of that, a hostile fixture whose entire file body is a runtime command envelope (schemaVersion/commandKind/leaseAuthority/requestDigest) must round-trip as base64 that decodes back to the original text, while `JSON.stringify(snapshot)` must contain neither "commandKind" nor "leaseAuthority" anywhere — proving the envelope stays inert content and never becomes structure. A final test asserts assignment to `snapshot.authority` throws TypeError, so frozen-ness is verified by behavior and not just by `Object.isFrozen`.

Fixture strings avoid the scheduler package-boundary literals; re-verified with the real regex over the package, 0 matches.

implementationPlan.description: Green — src/skill-loader.ts + src/skill-snapshot.ts + final src/index.ts exports. skill-loader.ts (target <=250): loadSkillBundle(bundleRoot, validatedManifest) — resolve realBundleRoot = realpathSync(bundleRoot) once (root may itself be a symlink/junction; that is fine, containment is against ITS realpath); per declared file: realpathSync(join) wrapped so ANY throw (ENOENT, device, revoked link) maps to SKILL_FILE_MISSING / fail-closed, containment check realFile.startsWith(realRoot + path.sep) (path.sep suffix mandatory — bare startsWith admits sibling-prefix dirs) else SKILL_SYMLINK_ESCAPE; read file ONCE via readFileSync, enforce byte caps on the READ bytes, sha256 the READ bytes, compare to manifest declaration (mismatch -> SKILL_DIGEST_MISMATCH; oversize -> SKILL_FILE_OVERSIZED); the read bytes are what flows onward — no re-stat, no re-read (kills TOCTOU). Read-only: zero writes anywhere. Injectable fs facade parameter (defaulting to node:fs) so containment/symlink logic is unit-testable without Developer-Mode symlink permissions. skill-snapshot.ts (target <=250): resolveSkillSnapshot(loadedBundles, requests) — explicit deterministic all-or-nothing resolution per the step-4 cases, output sorted by skillId; BYTES IMMUTABILITY STRATEGY (mandatory — Object.freeze on a non-empty Uint8Array THROWS): snapshot and renderer input store file content ONLY as base64 strings (contentBase64) plus sha256 + byteLength; no typed array is ever placed in the frozen graph and no function-typed values exist anywhere (getters would violate the no-function allowlist test); deep-freeze the whole graph; toSkillRendererInput(snapshot) -> frozen { rendererInputVersion, advisoryOnly: true, authority: "NONE", skills: [...] } — pure projection, no fs, no ambient state. index.ts exports ONLY the public surface: versions, limits, error codes, validateSkillManifestBytes, loadSkillBundle, resolveSkillSnapshot, toSkillRendererInput + public types via export type. All skill-bundle tests green; focused typecheck green. If any module crosses 400 lines despite the targets, split it and record the added file via the step note/amendment — do not blob past the rail.
implementationPlan.note:
GREEN. Typecheck exits 0; focused suite 2 files / 75 passed, 1 skipped. Production sizes: index 49, skill-contract 160, skill-snapshot 153, skill-loader 166, skill-manifest 222 — all well inside the 250 target, none near the 400 hard split.

skill-loader.ts. `isContained` appends `path.sep` when the root lacks it — the sibling-prefix test is exactly what a bare `startsWith` would wrongly admit. `resolveReal` swallows ANY realpath throw into `null` so ENOENT, device paths, and revoked links all become one closed SKILL_FILE_MISSING instead of propagating. The root is realpath'd once and containment is measured against ITS realpath, so a bundle root that is itself a junction works correctly. `readFileSync` is separately wrapped, because realpath succeeding does not guarantee the read will. Read-once is structural: the bytes returned by that single read are what get size-checked, hashed, and base64-encoded — there is no re-stat or second read anywhere, so no TOCTOU window exists. Zero write operations in the module.

Size check uses `content.byteLength !== declared.byteLength`, which catches under-length as well as over-length. A file shorter than declared would also fail the digest check, but failing on the length first gives the more specific error.

skill-snapshot.ts. Resolution is all-or-nothing and sorted by skillId, so neither bundle order nor request order can move the digest. `snapshotDigest` is computed over the body BEFORE the digest field is added, which keeps it well-defined (no self-reference). No Date, no env, no absolute path enters the output — the loader deliberately stores only the manifest-relative `path`, never `realFile`, so an absolute temp-dir path cannot leak into a digest and break replay.

BYTES NEVER ENTER THE FROZEN GRAPH. Content travels only as `contentBase64` plus sha256 and byteLength. This is not stylistic: `Object.freeze` on a non-empty Uint8Array throws TypeError, so a typed array in the graph would make `deepFreeze` throw at runtime. Defensive-copy getters were rejected for a second reason — a function-typed value would fail the no-function allowlist test in step 4. An empty file yields `contentBase64: ""`, which is why I added that assertion back in step 2.

Added one guard beyond the plan: a repeated skillId within the REQUEST list is SKILL_REQUEST_AMBIGUOUS. Without it, requesting the same skill twice would silently emit a duplicate snapshot entry, which is neither explicit nor deterministic-by-identity.

TYPECHECK CAUGHT A REAL DEFECT IN MY OWN TEST HELPER, not in production code: `expectFailure(result: { ok: boolean })` needed `result as { code: string }`, which tsc rejected with TS2352. A cast there would have been the wrong fix — it would let a success result silently reach the code assertion. Retyped the parameter as `{ readonly ok: true } | SkillFailure` so the literal flag discriminates and the helper narrows properly, with an explicit throw on the success branch. Every result union in the package is assignable to it.

The real-symlink test is SKIPPED on this host, and I verified why rather than assuming: a direct `symlinkSync` probe returns EPERM (no Developer Mode). The skip is legitimate and the containment logic is not left untested — the three injected-facade cases (sibling-prefix escape, genuine-inside accept, throwing-realpath) exercise the same predicate deterministically on any host. On a machine with Developer Mode the fourth test also runs. Flagging so QA does not read "1 skipped" as a coverage hole.

planningNotes.risks: (1) Windows path hostility is the core attack surface: colon anywhere (ADS streams), reserved device stems (CON.md resolves to the device), trailing dot/space (Win32 strips — breaks duplicate detection), case-insensitive collisions, non-NFC identity collisions — all must be rejected at MANIFEST validation, before any fs touch. (2) Symlink containment: compare realpath(file) to realpath(bundleRoot)+path.sep (bare startsWith admits skills-evil/ siblings; unresolved root string breaks when root itself is a junction); every realpath/read throw maps to a stable fail-closed code. TOCTOU: read once, hash the read bytes, snapshot those bytes. (3) Determinism: no Date.now/capturedAt/env/absolute paths anywhere in snapshot or provenance (phase0-evidence-contract.ts:88 capturedAt is the tempting WRONG precedent); canonical serialization is sorted-key, integer-only. (4) Windows CI may lack symlink permission (EPERM without Developer Mode) — loader takes an injectable fs facade so containment logic is unit-tested without real symlinks; real-symlink test uses a capability probe + skipIf. (5) Authority neutrality must be the allowlist deep-walk (exact keys, deep isFrozen, no functions, hostile envelope stays inert string) — a forbidden-key denylist is unfalsifiable theater. (6) Shared dirty tree: temp fixtures only under os.tmpdir(); wrapper auto-commit sweeps repo-root strays (mem:gotcha-moe-wrapper-autocommit).
